graders.evidence:
I couldn't fetch the vetted accessibility cards. The first fetch was blocked by the network allowlist, and Bash is now denied in this session. The checks below are therefore my own manual review of `form.jsx`, not a card-by-card ledger. Nothing here is marked PASS against a card.

## Accessibility review: `form.jsx` (16 lines, all read)

**Verdict: request changes.** Three issues would block merge in my judgment.

### FAIL (blocking)

1. **The submit control is a `<div>`, not a button** (`form.jsx:11-13`).
   - A `div` has no role, isn't focusable, and doesn't respond to Enter or Space. Keyboard and screen-reader users can't submit via the button.
   - Fix: `<button type="submit">Sign up</button>`.
   - The `onClick={onSubmit}` is then redundant. It would also double-fire alongside the form's `onSubmit`, so remove it.

2. **The input has no accessible name** (`form.jsx:5-10`).
   - A `placeholder` isn't a reliable label. It disappears on input, usually has poor contrast, and isn't consistently announced.
   - Fix: add a visible `<label htmlFor="email">Email address</label>` with a matching `id="email"` on the input. If the design truly forbids a visible label, `aria-label` is the fallback.

3. **Mouse-only interaction** (`form.jsx:11`).
   - This is the same root cause as item 1: `onClick` on a non-interactive element gives no keyboard path and no focus indicator. Using a real `<button>` fixes it.

### Should-fix

4. **Missing autofill and input hints** (`form.jsx:5-6`). Add `autoComplete="email"` and `name="email"`. That helps users with motor or cognitive disabilities, and the purpose of the field becomes programmatically determinable.
5. **No error or status messaging.** The component shows no validation or submission feedback. If errors are added later, associate them with the input via `aria-describedby` and announce them with `role="alert"` or an `aria-live` region. Mark the field `required` if it is.

### Not assessable
- **Colour contrast and focus-ring styling:** the `.btn` CSS isn't in this file. Check that a visible `:focus-visible` style exists once it becomes a `<button>`.

### Suggested corrected markup
```jsx
<form onSubmit={onSubmit}>
  <label htmlFor="email">Email address</label>
  <input
    id="email"
    name="email"
    type="email"
    autoComplete="email"
    required
    value={email}
    onChange={(e) => setEmail(e.target.value)}
  />
  <button type="submit" className="btn">Sign up</button>
</form>
```

If you want the formal card-based ledger, I need network access to goodcodereview.com. Alternatively, you can paste `accessibility.md` here and I'll redo the review against it.

graders.evidence:
I couldn't fetch the vetted card list. The skill's step 1 needs `curl` against goodcodereview.com, and Bash is denied in this session (don't-ask mode). So the findings below come from my own reading of `form.jsx`, not from the cards. They have no card IDs or card severities. I've used "block" or "should-fix" as my own judgment, so please don't treat them as official card verdicts.

**Concern: accessibility. Own judgment, not card-backed.**

| Check | Result | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Interactive control uses a native, semantic element | **FAIL** (block) | `form.jsx:11-13`: the submit control is `<div className="btn" onClick=…>`. It has no button role. It can't be reached with Tab. Enter and Space don't activate it. Screen readers don't announce it as a button. Use `<button type="submit">Sign up</button>`. |
| Form controls have an accessible name | **FAIL** (block) | `form.jsx:5-10`: the email `<input>` has no `<label>`, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`. `placeholder` is not a reliable name. It disappears once the user types, and its contrast is often too low. Add a visible `<label htmlFor>` with a matching `id`. |
| Keyboard operability | **FAIL** (block) | `form.jsx:11`: the `div` has no `tabIndex`, no key handler and no role. Switching to a real `<button>` fixes this. |
| No duplicate or conflicting submit handling | **FAIL** (should-fix) | `form.jsx:4` and `form.jsx:11`: `onSubmit` is bound to both the form and the click handler. Once the control is a real submit button, drop the `onClick`. Keeping it would fire the handler twice. |
| Input purpose and autofill hints | **FAIL** (should-fix) | `form.jsx:5-6`: there is no `autoComplete="email"` and no `name`. Add both (WCAG 1.3.5). |
| Error and status messaging | N/A - not read | The file has no validation or error UI. If you add errors later, use `aria-invalid`, `aria-describedby`, and a live region. |
| Focus styling and colour contrast | N/A - not read | The CSS for `.btn` and the input isn't in this file. I can't judge it. |

**Verdict: request changes.** There are three blocking issues, all in the sign-up flow. The control isn't a button, the input has no label, and keyboard users can't submit the form.

Suggested fix:

```jsx
<form onSubmit={onSubmit}>
  <label htmlFor="signup-email">Email address</label>
  <input
    id="signup-email"
    name="email"
    type="email"
    autoComplete="email"
    required
    value={email}
    onChange={(e) => setEmail(e.target.value)}
  />
  <button type="submit">Sign up</button>
</form>
```

If you allow Bash, or let me fetch the cards another way, I'll re-run the review against the official cards and send back a proper ledger.

graders.name: scope
graders.evidence:
**Accessibility review of `form.jsx`: request changes.** I couldn't fetch the vetted card list from goodcodereview.com. The first attempt was rejected by the sandbox allowlist and the retry was denied by the permission mode. The checks below are my own reading of the 16 lines, not the vetted cards. They have no card IDs or card severities, and the severities shown are my own judgment.

## Verdict: request changes (2 blocking FAILs)

| Check | Result | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Interactive control uses a native element | **FAIL** (block) | `form.jsx:11-13`: the submit control is a `<div onClick>`. It isn't focusable, has no button role, and doesn't respond to Enter or Space. Keyboard and screen-reader users can't submit the form. |
| Form control has an accessible name | **FAIL** (block) | `form.jsx:5-10`: the email input has only a `placeholder`. It has no `<label>`, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`. Placeholders vanish on input, often have low contrast, and aren't reliably announced as names. |
| Submit works without a pointer | **FAIL** (should-fix) | `form.jsx:4,11`: `onSubmit` is bound to both the form and the div's `onClick`. Mouse users trigger it twice if the div is inside the form's submit path. Keyboard users get no working path from the div. Fixing the button fixes this too. |
| Input purpose and autofill | **FAIL** (should-fix) | `form.jsx:5-6`: there is no `autoComplete="email"` and no `name`. Autofill is the standard way to meet the identify-input-purpose requirement (WCAG 1.3.5). |
| Error and status feedback | N/A | There is no validation or error UI in this file. Add `aria-invalid` and `aria-describedby` with a live region when errors are introduced. |
| Contrast, focus styles | N/A - not read | The `.btn` CSS isn't in this file. Check that it doesn't use `outline: none`. |
| Headings, landmarks, language | N/A | The component is too small for these to apply. |

## Suggested fix

```jsx
<form onSubmit={onSubmit}>
  <label htmlFor="signup-email">Email address</label>
  <input
    id="signup-email"
    name="email"
    type="email"
    autoComplete="email"
    required
    value={email}
    onChange={(e) => setEmail(e.target.value)}
  />
  <button type="submit" className="btn">Sign up</button>
</form>
```

A native `<button type="submit">` makes the form's `onSubmit` the single submit path. You can then drop the `onClick`. You can keep a placeholder as a hint, but not as the only label.

**Outside this review:** `useState` is used without an import (`form.jsx:2`). That's a correctness issue, not an accessibility one.

If you want the vetted card ruleset applied, allow the fetch of `https://goodcodereview.com/concerns/accessibility.md` (or run it from an environment that permits it) and I'll redo the ledger against the cards.
